posts.author: jeff-blyth
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Well, unexpected result. At least for me. ...........................................The next set of holograms is an obect with all variables kept the same except the one on the right was soaked for 25 seconds in water prior to fixing and subsiquent steps. Very Broadband.

I think the broadbandedness seems to prove something of what I have been saying on my "apples vs oranges " thread.

The water soak which you did with presumably mild agitation on the whole plate, was long enough to have removed virtually all the unbroken dichromate buried in the dark zones in your gelatin layer. This leaves the 

light struck zones chemically holding onto the degraded dichromate and the dark zones swelling up in a virtually unhardened state. This has led to "chirped fringes" which are not sinusoidal but have a "top hat" profile

which makes for good brightness for HIGS (holographic image generators but bad for HOE's that are wanted for wavelength replay purity). I think the green areas in the left hand image are interesting too

as they look like a definite liquid involvement and not a temperature effect. 

The green bits suggest to me that they were areas where the fix got to work on making all the unaltered dichromate ions turn into Cr+++ hardener while still inside the gelatin layer whereas the less green parts 

were already loosing unconverted dichromate ions to solution. So what caused this differential effect ?

jeff

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md: I think before the fix hardener agent you simply "insuflated" (swelling up) the gelatin with the water bath and with the detergent help that applied 'wetting' to the gelatin so the x-link step hardening were applied to expanded fringes that were after xlinked with hardener in this state before drying.

posts.author: jeff-blyth
posts.content_md:
> **Sergio:** I think before the fix hardener agent you simply "insuflated" (swelling up) the gelatin with the water bath and with the detergent help that applied 'wetting' to the gelatin so the x-link step hardening were applied toexpanded fringesthat were after xlinked with hardener in this state before drying.

Yes Sergio that is yet another point for us to think on. The literature(particularly from Lessard's Canadian group shows that initially the light struck DCG makes Cr V and this appears to bind to the gelatin without properly crosslinking it. It needs to be turned into Cr III before the hardening is complete. So that

means swelling up more before completing X linking and then that will have a different effect than if it is more crosslinked before the swelling is

greater. -----No wonder people in earlier days who tried to make consistent DCG images for a living had near nervous breakdowns!

jeff
